headline: WEEK 11: DAK DETONATES, THE PENIX STANDS TALL, AND TWO GAMES END IN PURE ASS-CLENCHING CHAOS
html:
WEEK 11: DAK DETONATES, THE PENIX STANDS TALL, AND TWO GAMES END IN PURE ASS-CLENCHING CHAOS

Week 11 kicked down the door, drank the good liquor, and left five different managers staring at lineup screens like they had just discovered numbers can hurt. Kirkumcised Penix posted the week’s highest score at 166.96, while Dak Prescott delivered a 35.9-point flamethrower and Jonah Coleman nearly ran through the earth’s crust.

The weekly median was 130.29. Kirkumcised Penix, alexvandeusen, RoCknCoCk Crashouts , I didnt hear no bell, and Chase’n Skattehoes earned median wins. Everyone else ate a median loss, including OguguaAnunoby despite escaping head-to-head by 3.26 points. The biggest win belonged to I didnt hear no bell by 38.76; the closest game was OguguaAnunoby’s 3.26-point survival over Pukakke.

1. THE PENIX DROPS 166.96 AND LEAVES ALEX IN THE SPLASH ZONE

Kirkumcised Penix defeated alexvandeusen, 166.96–134.46, by 32.50 points. This was the week’s highest team score and a complete offensive gangbang. CeeDee Lamb led the operation with 30.2 points on 11 catches, 132 yards, and a touchdown. Travis Kelce added 25.4 with six receptions, 74 yards, and two scores, while Derrick Henry supplied 19.1 despite losing a fumble.

alexvandeusen did not play badly. Javonte Williams produced 24.1 points with 67 rushing yards and two total touchdowns, Jared Goff scored 23.36 on 279 passing yards and two touchdowns, and Breece Hall added 19.0. But the Minnesota defense scored 0.0 after allowing 29 points, which is less “defense” and more ten traffic cones wearing matching helmets.

The bench also featured Ladd McConkey’s eligible 20.7 points, including two receiving touchdowns, while Jaylen Waddle managed 9.1 in a starting WR slot. That swap alone would not have erased 32.50, but it would have made the body look less bloated at the funeral. Both teams still beat the 130.29 median, so alexvandeusen took the head-to-head loss without surrendering the week’s second result.

Verdict: Kirkumcised Penix brought Lamb, Kelce, Henry, Cook, Flowers, and a 16-point San Francisco defense to a knife fight. alexvandeusen brought a respectable lineup and got launched through a fucking window anyway.

2. DAK PRESCOTT PUTS ARUPERT12 THROUGH THE WINDSHIELD

RoCknCoCk Crashouts defeated arupert12, 145.40–109.66, by 35.74 points. Dak Prescott was the engine, the gasoline, and the asshole throwing the match: 35.9 fantasy points from 325 passing yards, four passing touchdowns, and another score on the ground. DJ Moore added 23.1 on eight catches, 91 yards, and a touchdown, while Malik Nabers scored 18.5.

arupert12 never found a comparable eruption. David Montgomery led the team with 15.4 points on 107 rushing yards and three catches. Josh Allen threw for 304 yards but scored only 14.16 after one touchdown and two interceptions. Jonathan Taylor’s 21 rushing yards produced 6.7 points, and Jaylen Warren contributed 4.9. That backfield performed like somebody had poured concrete into its cleats.

Carnell Tate’s 16.8 points sat on arupert12’s bench while eligible WR and flex starters Josh Downs and Tee Higgins scored 9.9 and 12.3. It was a supported bench miss, but not the cause of a 35.74-point demolition. RoCknCoCk Crashouts beat both arupert12 and the median; arupert12 lost both.

Verdict: Dak supplied five touchdowns. arupert12 supplied sadness, two Allen interceptions, and a lineup that never crossed 16 points at any position. This was less a matchup than a public tire rotation performed on a human torso.

Highlight: Dak Prescott (35.90 fantasy points) — Game coverage (individual scoring clip unavailable): ESPN game coverage

3. “I DIDNT HEAR NO BELL” HEARD SECRET SERVICE CHAT HIT THE FLOOR

I didnt hear no bell defeated Secret service chat, 135.66–96.90, by 38.76 points. That was the biggest win of Week 11. Chuba Hubbard bulldozed his way to 26.0 points with 120 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Patrick Mahomes added 24.96 on 324 passing yards and three scores, while Chris Olave delivered 19.2 with nine receptions and 102 yards.

Secret service chat got 24.3 from Emmett Johnson on 105 rushing yards, 38 receiving yards, and a touchdown. Joe Burrow scored 19.9 with 300 passing yards and two touchdowns, and the Chicago defense added 17.0 through six sacks and two takeaways. Then the rest of the lineup collectively crawled into a storm drain: Tank Dell and Elic Ayomanor each scored 5.7, Jordyn Tyson scored 2.0, and Juwan Johnson posted a zero on one target.

I didnt hear no bell even survived Courtland Sutton’s 0.0 in a flex slot. Jalen Coker’s eligible 8.7 points were left on the bench, but a 38.76-point margin turns that decision from “lineup crime” into “harmless drunken paperwork.” The winner cleared the median; Secret service chat missed it by 33.39 points and took losses in both formats.

Verdict: Secret service chat had three excellent scores and seven positions full of wet cardboard. Hubbard and Mahomes handled the execution while Olave and Shakir helped bury the evidence.

Highlight: Chuba Hubbard (26.00 fantasy points) — Game coverage (individual scoring clip unavailable): ESPN game coverage

4. CHEF BOYARDEE LEAVES MIKE EVANS IN THE CAN AND LOSES BY 4.50

Chase’n Skattehoes defeated Chef Boyardee, 132.54–128.04, by 4.50 points. Jonah Coleman was the week’s most violent individual starter, scoring 34.9 points on 111 rushing yards, three touchdowns, and four receptions. Antonio Williams added 21.2 from nine catches and 122 yards, while Tyler Bass somehow chipped in 17.0 points as a kicker because fantasy football enjoys humiliating us.

Chef Boyardee countered with George Pickens at 23.8, Jameson Williams at 22.3, and Parker Washington at 18.3. Those three combined for 298 receiving yards and two touchdowns. But Tyler Warren scored 3.2, Garrett Wilson managed 6.9, and the lineup left Mike Evans’ 22.9 eligible WR points on the bench. Evans had six catches, 109 yards, and a touchdown. Starting him over Wilson would have added 16.0 points and flipped the game. That is not hindsight; that is a certified lineup felony with fingerprints on the knife.

Chase’n Skattehoes also benched C.J. Stroud’s 22.46 for Caleb Williams’ 15.34 and Chimere Dike’s 13.3 while Xavier Hutchinson scored 3.3. The winner left plenty of points unused but still cleared the 130.29 median by 2.25. Chef Boyardee lost head-to-head and missed the median by 2.25, the fantasy equivalent of watching both elevators close while your pants are caught in one.

Verdict: Jonah Coleman saved Chase’n Skattehoes from its own lineup wobbling. Chef Boyardee had the winning ingredients sitting on the counter and somehow served a bowl of hot defeat.

Highlight: Jonah Coleman (34.90 fantasy points) — Player scoring highlight: Jonah Coleman punches in a TD for Denver

5. OGUGUA ESCAPES PUKAKKE BY 3.26 IN THE WEEK’S TIGHTEST SHITSHOW

OguguaAnunoby defeated Pukakke, 110.16–106.90, by 3.26 points. This was Week 11’s closest game, a low-scoring crawl through broken glass. Jahmyr Gibbs carried OguguaAnunoby with 27.8 points from 98 rushing yards, 20 receiving yards, and two touchdowns. Tetairoa McMillan scored 19.1, and George Kittle converted three catches into 34 yards, two touchdowns, and 18.4 points.

Pukakke nearly stole it behind Ashton Jeanty’s 30.9-point masterpiece: 79 rushing yards, five catches, 90 receiving yards, and a touchdown. Bucky Irving added 19.0, but Kirk Cousins produced only 8.4 with 235 passing yards, no touchdowns, and an interception. Caleb Douglas caught two of 10 targets for 30 yards, while Emeka Egbuka scored 3.8. That is a receiving corps attempting CPR with oven mitts.

The fatal mistake was Jacory Croskey-Merritt’s 15.7 eligible RB/flex points sitting on Pukakke’s bench. Aaron Jones Sr. scored 11.3 and Egbuka scored 3.8 in the flex mix; replacing Egbuka with Croskey-Merritt would have added 11.9 and won the matchup. OguguaAnunoby was hardly clean: DK Metcalf scored 1.2, Spencer Shrader went one-for-three on field goals for 1.0, and Pat Freiermuth’s eligible 9.0 sat behind two struggling flex plays.

Neither team reached the 130.29 median, so OguguaAnunoby earned the head-to-head win but still took a median loss. Pukakke lost both and fell to a current 3-19, a record that looks like a distress signal punched into a calculator.

Verdict: OguguaAnunoby survived because Gibbs and Kittle built a raft out of touchdowns. Pukakke left the winning lineup on the bench and drowned three feet from shore.

Highlight: Ashton Jeanty (30.90 fantasy points) — Game coverage (individual scoring clip unavailable): ESPN game coverage

POWER METER SUMMARY

  • Kirkumcised Penix: Power score 93. The current 15-7 record, Week 11-leading 166.96, and balanced Daniels-Lamb-Cook-Henry-Flowers-Kelce core make this the league’s loudest monster.
  • alexvandeusen: Power score 90. Also 15-7 with 1,605.12 points and serious depth, though the Week 11 beating showed that depth cannot tackle CeeDee Lamb.
  • OguguaAnunoby: Power score 87. League-leading 1,623.84 points and a 14-8 record remain elite, even after barely squeezing past the last-place team.
  • RoCknCoCk Crashouts : Power score 84. A 14-8 record and 145.40-point Week 11 prove this roster can do more than possess an aggressively capitalized name.
  • Secret service chat: Power score 75. Strong total scoring remains, but 96.90 in Week 11 was a ceiling collapse with paperwork still inside.
  • Chase’n Skattehoes: Power score 69. The current .500 record keeps the leash tight, but Coleman’s eruption delivered a crucial win.
  • I didnt hear no bell: Power score 65. Also .500, but a 135.66-point double win keeps the bell from becoming a funeral bell.
  • arupert12: Power score 61. The star names remain impressive; the current 8-14 record and 109.66-point week remain very much not.
  • Chef Boyardee: Power score 51. Talent exists, but the current 7-15 record and Evans bench disaster taste like canned regret.
  • Pukakke: Power score 29. Jeanty and Irving flashed real upside, but 3-19 and a league-low 1,211.20 points are an anchor tied directly to the nuts.

FRAUD WATCH

OguguaAnunoby remains third on the official board, but beating Pukakke by only 3.26 while scoring 110.16 earns an immediate customs inspection. The roster has the league’s most points overall, so this is not a fraud conviction. It is merely an officer shining a flashlight into the trunk and asking why DK Metcalf scored 1.2.

STOCK UP

  • Kirkumcised Penix: Week-high 166.96, two wins, and sole ownership of the week’s biggest offensive flex.
  • RoCknCoCk Crashouts : Dak’s 35.9 powered a 35.74-point win and another median victory.
  • I didnt hear no bell: Biggest margin of the week, a median win, and a current 11-11 record instead of sinking below .500.
  • Chase’n Skattehoes: Won the close game and cleared the median despite leaving useful points on the bench.

STOCK DOWN

  • Secret service chat: A 96.90-point crater and losses both head-to-head and against the median.
  • arupert12: Four starters below 10 points and a 35.74-point paddling.
  • Chef Boyardee: Lost by 4.50 while Mike Evans’ 22.9 watched from the bench like the only sober person at a DUI checkpoint.
  • Pukakke: Came within 3.26 of an upset, then discovered the winning points were sitting beside the coach.

OFFICIAL WEEK 11 SHITSHOW AWARDS

  • Player of the Week — Dak Prescott, 35.9 points: He completed 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns, then added a rushing score because arupert12 apparently had not suffered enough.
  • Team of the Week — Kirkumcised Penix, 166.96: Lamb scored 30.2, Kelce scored 25.4, and seven starters reached double figures. This lineup did not win; it annexed territory.
  • Biggest Disaster — Secret service chat: A 96.90 total, a 38.76-point loss, and four offensive starters at 5.7 or lower. The Bears defense nearly outscored seven teammates by itself.
  • Closest-Game Survivor — OguguaAnunoby: Won by 3.26 despite DK Metcalf and Spencer Shrader combining for 2.2 points. Gibbs deserves hazard pay.
  • Lineup Crime — Chef Boyardee: Mike Evans scored 22.9 on the bench while Garrett Wilson scored 6.9 as a starter. The resulting 16-point swing would have erased a 4.50-point loss with room to spare.
  • Bench Blunder — Pukakke: Jacory Croskey-Merritt scored 15.7 on the bench while Emeka Egbuka posted 3.8 in a flex slot. That eligible swap would have flipped the closest game of the week.

FINAL WORD FROM SBF NETWORK

The supplied standings are current standings that may postdate this historical Week 11 recap. They show Kirkumcised Penix and alexvandeusen tied at 15-7, OguguaAnunoby and RoCknCoCk Crashouts at 14-8, and six playoff spots available with the postseason beginning in Week 15. Secret service chat currently holds fifth at 12-10, while Chase’n Skattehoes and I didnt hear no bell are knotted at 11-11 around the sixth-place knife fight.

That makes every upcoming head-to-head and median result a two-pronged kick to the standings. The leaders are fighting for control, the middle is fighting for oxygen, and the bottom is fighting to avoid becoming a cautionary screenshot in next year’s draft room. Set your lineups, check the flex eligibility, and for the love of all that is holy, stop leaving game-winning receivers on the fucking bench.
